task.instruction: Find the top story from BBC News in the technology section for today.

final_answer:
The top story on BBC News's Technology page (bbc.com/technology) is "Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe". The page lists it first, and its browser title is "Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears".

This story is not strictly from today. It was published "21 hours ago", and it is now Saturday, 7 November 2026, 6:55 PM GMT+8. That puts it on Friday, 6 November. The Cybertruck item below it was posted 20 hours ago. I found nothing on the Technology page that was clearly published today, so this is the top story the section shows today, and it is the most recent one.

The article says global stock markets fell after investors sold tech shares. They feared the US midterm elections would slow AI development. The sell-off began in the US and spread to Asia and Europe. Trillions of dollars were wiped off major tech firms' stock values. The Nasdaq sank 5.5% on Thursday. The so-called "magnificent seven" tech companies lost about a trillion dollars in one trading day, and Nvidia shares fell more than 9%. Tesla fell nearly 11% and SpaceX fell 8%. Investors are worried about tougher AI regulation, because Democrat candidates opposed the data centres the technology needs. There are also doubts about whether the huge spending on AI will pay off.

Link: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmn04705rd8jo

judge.rationale: The BBC Technology page text shows the first listed story as “Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe,” which the agent reported with link.

final_page.title: Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears
